name: arc-match-shapes-to-framed-holes
description: Use when an ARC grid has repeated monochrome framed cells and detached colored shapes. Match shape silhouettes to frame cutouts and place them.
---

# Match detached shapes to framed holes

When a grid has repeated regions made from a common frame color, plus detached colored objects elsewhere:

1. Identify the repeated frame regions (often separated by full-width rows/columns of the frame color) and the non-frame colored objects.
2. For each region, record its interior cutout as a binary silhouette: occupied/empty positions, ignoring colors. Include all interior holes, not just the count.
3. Record each detached object as a binary silhouette, ignoring its color. Normalize only for translation; preserve orientation unless a demonstrated rule indicates rotation/reflection.
4. Match each framed cutout with the detached object having the identical silhouette. Recolor the cutout with that object's color; preserve the frame color and its dimensions. This may reorder objects relative to their initial positions.
5. Remove the detached-object area if the output format/demo indicates only the framed regions remain. Confirm output dimensions and all rows against the frame layout.

Key diagnostic: objects and cutouts can have equal cell counts but differ in arrangement, so match the full pattern rather than area or object order. Use a demonstration to establish whether rotations/reflections are allowed and whether the detached region is discarded.",
